sentences.text: Glikmanius was an extinct cartilaginous fish belonging to the subclass Elasmobranchii, the order Ctenacanthiformes, and the family Ctenacanthidae.
The species Glikmanius occidentalis may have exceeded six meters in length, making it one of the largest marine predators of its time.

The genus was named in honor of Dr. Leonid Glikman, who first suggested its link to ctenacanthiforms, while fossils from the Carboniferous Pottsville Formation in Alabama were described by Egli in 2026.
Skeletal remains of this animal have also been found in Nebraska, USA.
The type species is Glikmanius occidentalis, originally described by Leidy in 1859, and three species are currently recognized within the genus: G. culmenis, G. myachovensis, and G. careforum.
Glikmanius lived during the Carboniferous and Permian periods in North America and Russia, spanning the Moscovian to Wuchiapingian stages between 315.2 and 254.14 million years ago.
